The final assertion of the lemma holds by
Topology, Lemma <REF_0001>.
The equivalence of (5) and (1) is
Topology, Lemma <REF_0002>.
Hence, using Lemma <REF_0003>,
we see that (1) <MATH_0001> (2).
To finish proving the lemma it suffices to show that ``Jacobson''
is a local property of rings, see Lemma <REF_0004>.
Any localization of a Jacobson ring at an element is Jacobson, see
Algebra, Lemma <REF_0005>.
Suppose <MATH_0002> is a ring, <MATH_0003> generate the unit
ideal and each <MATH_0004> is Jacobson. Then we see that
<MATH_0005> is a union of open subsets
which are all Jacobson, and hence <MATH_0006> is Jacobson
by Topology, Lemma <REF_0006> again.
This proves the second property of Definition <REF_0007>.
